courses.title: Water Mitigation New-Hire Fundamentals
courses.description: The complete interactive water mitigation onboarding course supplied by Rainbow Restoration, including ten instructional modules, a final assessment, hands-on competency evaluation, and certificate.
courses.credentialWarning: Internal training only; not an IICRC WRT certification.

courses.title: Respiratory Protection Interactive Training
courses.description: The complete supplied respiratory protection course with medical-evaluation and fit-testing prerequisites, respirator selection, use, care, task-specific hazards, exam, practical evaluation, acknowledgment, and annual certificate.
courses.credentialWarning: Course completion does not authorize respirator use without current medical clearance, fit testing, assigned equipment, and program authorization.

courses.title: Water Loss Safety & Initial Response
courses.description: How to make a new water loss safe, confirm source status, protect occupants, establish work zones, and recognize immediate stop-work conditions.
courses.regulatoryBasis: 29 CFR 1926.21; 29 CFR 1926 Subparts C, D, E, and K
objectives: Explain safety, source control, occupant protection, utilities, contamination, and structural conditions are evaluated before production work.
Apply the approved Rainbow Restoration work sequence for water loss safety & initial response.
Recognize stop-work conditions and create a complete training or job record.

lessons.title: Purpose, scope, and learning objectives
lessons.summary: How to make a new water loss safe, confirm source status, protect occupants, establish work zones, and recognize immediate stop-work conditions.
bullets: Explain safety, source control, occupant protection, utilities, contamination, and structural conditions are evaluated before production work.
Apply the approved Rainbow Restoration work sequence for water loss safety & initial response.
Recognize stop-work conditions and create a complete training or job record.
lessons.callout: This is internal company training. Follow current company programs, site-specific instructions, manufacturer information, and applicable law.

lessons.title: Recognize the hazard or work condition
lessons.summary: Technicians must understand the conditions that control the work before beginning water loss safety & initial response.
bullets: Safety, source control, occupant protection, utilities, contamination, and structural conditions are evaluated before production work.
A wet ceiling, energized equipment, chemical odor, unstable surface, or unknown contamination can require immediate withdrawal and escalation.
The affected boundary is determined by inspection and measurement, not by visible staining alone.
lessons.callout: When the condition cannot be confidently classified or controlled, pause the task and obtain supervisor or competent-person review.

lessons.title: Approved field workflow
lessons.summary: Use a repeatable sequence that protects people, property, evidence, and the job record.
bullets: Complete a site-specific safety review before disturbing materials.
Confirm the source, affected boundaries, contamination conditions, and the approved scope.
Use the assigned extraction, drying, cleaning, or removal procedure and reassess when conditions change.
Record readings, photographs, equipment, decisions, communications, and exceptions in company systems.
lessons.callout: Never bypass a required survey, authorization, medical clearance, fit test, license, competent person, or equipment inspection.

lessons.title: Documentation, verification, and closeout
lessons.summary: The record must show what was found, what was decided, what was done, and who verified completion.
bullets: Initial conditions and source notes
Moisture map and daily readings
Equipment or work performed
Photos, authorizations, and closeout notes
lessons.callout: Course completion documents internal training only and does not replace a license, outside certification, or site-specific authorization when one is required.

quiz.question: Which statement is a key principle of Water Loss Safety & Initial Response?
options: Safety, source control, occupant protection, utilities, contamination, and structural conditions are evaluated before production work.
Begin work before evaluating hazards so production is not delayed.
Use the same controls on every project without reassessment.
Rely only on memory instead of the approved procedure.
quiz.rationale: Safety, source control, occupant protection, utilities, contamination, and structural conditions are evaluated before production work.

quiz.question: What is the correct response when conditions are unknown, outside the approved scope, or cannot be safely controlled?
options: Continue briefly and reassess later.
Stop work, protect the area, and notify the supervisor or designated competent person.
Ask the customer to select the PPE.
Remove the material before photographing it.
quiz.rationale: Unknown or uncontrolled conditions require stop-work, isolation when needed, and reassessment by an authorized person.

quiz.question: Which action belongs in the approved work sequence for this course?
options: Skip the pre-task review when the job is urgent.
Complete a site-specific safety review before disturbing materials.
Discard damaged equipment only after the shift.
Change the scope without communicating the reason.
quiz.rationale: Complete a site-specific safety review before disturbing materials.

quiz.question: Which item supports a defensible training or job record?
options: An undocumented verbal assumption.
Initial conditions and source notes
Deleting photographs that show changed conditions.
Entering all rooms under one generic note.
quiz.rationale: The record should include initial conditions and source notes and other course-specific documentation.

quiz.question: Does completion of this internal LMS course, by itself, grant a government license, third-party certification, medical clearance, fit test, or authorization for regulated work?
options: Yes, for all restoration work.
Yes, when the quiz score is 100 percent.
No. Separate prerequisites and task-specific authorization still apply.
Only when the employee prints the certificate.
quiz.rationale: Internal course completion is only one part of qualification and does not replace external credentials or site-specific authorization.

Stop work, protect the area, and notify the supervisor or designated competent person.
Ask the customer to select the PPE.
Remove the material before photographing it.
quiz.rationale: Unknown or uncontrolled conditions require stop-work, isolation when needed, and reassessment by an authorized person.

quiz.question: Which action belongs in the approved work sequence for this course?
options: Skip the pre-task review when the job is urgent.
Identify the applicable program, competent person, records, and employee groups.
Discard damaged equipment only after the shift.
Change the scope without communicating the reason.
quiz.rationale: Identify the applicable program, competent person, records, and employee groups.

quiz.question: Which item supports a defensible training or job record?
options: An undocumented verbal assumption.
Program review and responsible person
Deleting photographs that show changed conditions.
Entering all rooms under one generic note.
quiz.rationale: The record should include program review and responsible person and other course-specific documentation.

quiz.question: Does completion of this internal LMS course, by itself, grant a government license, third-party certification, medical clearance, fit test, or authorization for regulated work?
options: Yes, for all restoration work.
Yes, when the quiz score is 100 percent.
No. Separate prerequisites and task-specific authorization still apply.
Only when the employee prints the certificate.
quiz.rationale: Internal course completion is only one part of qualification and does not replace external credentials or site-specific authorization.
